title: Through Thee We Now Together Came
description: Through Thee We Now Together Came in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 922 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”, where the book credits them to the Methodist Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through thee we now to-ge-ther came, In sin-gle-ness of heart; We met, O, Je-sus, in thy name, And in thy name we part.

lines: Through thee we now together came,
We met, O, Jesus, in thy name,
And in thy name we part.
We part in body, not in mind;
And, each to each in Jesus joined,
We hand in hand go on.
Present we still in spirit are,
While on the wings of faith and prayer
Our life is hid with Christ in God;
And shed his glory all abroad

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
